overview.title: Passive Listening
overview.subtitle: Passive listeners accept data pushed by external systems. Open-source includes Webhook (HTTP/HTTPS) only; syslog / snmp / mqtt are extension-injected.
overview.desc: Passive listeners accept metrics, logs and event data pushed by external systems. The open-source edition includes a Webhook listener; Syslog / SNMP / MQTT listeners are extended by the extension via injection.
overview.webhookDesc: HTTP/HTTPS POST reporting, suitable for custom scripts and third-party integrations
overview.syslogDesc: RFC 5424 / 3164 log reporting, suitable for network devices and system services
overview.snmpDesc: SNMP v1/v2c/v3 Trap and Inform reporting, suitable for network device alerts
overview.mqttDesc: MQTT 3.1.1 / 5.0 subscription reporting, suitable for IoT devices and edge gateways
overview.eventEmptyDesc: No reporting data received yet, please refresh later
overview.toggleConfirmContent: External systems will not be able to push data after disabling. Are you sure?

webhook.title: Webhook Listener Configuration
webhook.endpointHelp: External systems push data to this endpoint via POST requests. The endpoint URL is auto-assigned.
webhook.methodHelp: Only POST method is supported, Content-Type is application/json
webhook.secretHelp: Used for HMAC signature verification, keep it safe. After regeneration, the old secret becomes invalid immediately and connected systems must update.
webhook.enableHelp: External systems cannot push data when disabled
webhook.authHmacDesc: Sender computes HMAC-SHA256 using the secret, transmits signature via X-Tickraft-Signature header
webhook.authAssetKeyDesc: Sender includes asset_key in request body, server verifies against known key sets
webhook.hmacDesc: HMAC-SHA256: The sender computes HMAC-SHA256 of the request body using the secret, puts the hex digest in the X-Tickraft-Signature header; the server recomputes and compares to verify before accepting data.
webhook.assetKeyDesc: Asset Key: The sender includes an asset_key field in the request body; the server verifies asset ownership against known key sets. Suitable for intranet or low-risk scenarios.
webhook.curlHmacHelp: When using HMAC, set the X-Tickraft-Signature header to the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the request body
webhook.curlAssetKeyHelp: When using Asset Key, include the asset_key field in the request body
webhook.hmacPrinciple: Compute HMAC-SHA256 of request body with secret, verify via X-Tickraft-Signature header
webhook.assetKeyPrinciple: Include asset_key in request body, server verifies against known key sets
webhook.hmacSecurity: Secret not transmitted with request, tamper-proof and replay-proof
webhook.assetKeySecurity: Secret transmitted with request, recommended for intranet only
webhook.assetKeyHeader: No extra header, secret in request body
webhook.hmacUseCase: Cross-network reporting, production environments, high-security scenarios
webhook.assetKeyUseCase: Intranet reporting, temporary debugging, simple integration
webhook.tipsItem1: Webhook endpoint is auto-assigned by the system, no manual path configuration needed
webhook.tipsItem2: HMAC-SHA256 is more secure, the secret is not transmitted with the request
webhook.tipsItem3: After regenerating, the old secret is invalidated immediately; all reporting systems must update
webhook.tipsItem4: HTTPS endpoint is recommended for production to ensure data transfer security
webhook.tipsItem5: Single request body size limit is 1MB; larger requests will be rejected
webhook.regenerateConfirmContent: After regeneration, the old secret becomes invalid immediately. All connected reporting systems must update the secret, otherwise data reporting will be rejected. Continue?
webhook.regenerateSuccess: Signing secret regenerated, please sync to reporting systems
